newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU WEAKENS VS DLR, SEEN SLIDING FURTHER.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU WEAKENS VS DLR, SEEN SLIDING FURTHER.

text.p: Romania's leu dipped to 6,350/400 to the dollar at Thursday's close after idling at 6,150/200 in the morning on a market still digesting the jump in the one-week refinancing rate to 90 percent from 81 percent.
Traders said that for the first time in months leu-dollar retail prices, which bobbed around 6,050/350, were firmer than interbank rates, as currency shops were facing leu shortages.
They said intrabank trading saw a higher hard currency offer, but the overall market remained short, with exporters awaiting fresh leu-dollar lows.
"The leu might get some support from Thursday's rise in the one-week rate. But most hard currency holders still fancy lower leu levels," said one trader.
"We may see the leu at 6,500 tomorrow and heading towards 6,900 by the end of the month," said another.

The money market became illiquid after Thursday's rate hike with traders awaiting further rises in the central bank's key rates, the discount and the Lombard rate -- now at an annual 50 and 90 percent respectively.

"The Lombard rate is usually the highest of the central bank's rates," said one trader, adding that the bank might soon bring discount and Lombard rates in line with its recent tighter monetary policy.

The central bank's recent moves are aimed to temper surging inflation and to restrain the expansion of money supply in a bid to prop up the sagging leu, which lost more than 50 percent against the dollar since January 1.
Year-on-year inflation rose to 56.9 percent last December, nearly triple the 20 percent 1996 target agreed with the International Monetary Fund.

Earlier on Thursday short-term rates lingered near 80 percent but traders said the money market was expected higher prices as major banks were chasing leu funds. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
